lessons.title: Hello Python & Variables
lessons.summary: Learn how to display output with print(), store data in variables, and format text using f-strings.
lessons.conceptHtml:
Welcome to Python!

Python is one of the most popular and readable programming languages in the world. Let's start with two core building blocks:

  • print() displays text, numbers, or calculation results on the screen.
  • Variables store information (like text strings, whole numbers int, or decimals float) so you can reuse them.
  • f-strings (formatted strings) let you embed variables directly inside text using f"Hello {name}!".
Example
student = "Aarav"
score = 95
print(f"{student} scored {score}% in Python!")
lessons.starterCode:
# Lesson 1: Hello Python & Variables
# Click "Run Code" (or press Ctrl+Enter) to execute via WebSocket!

language = "Python"
version = 3.14
is_fun = True

print("🐍 Welcome to the Online Python Learning Lab!")
print(f"Currently learning: {language} (v{version})")
print(f"Is coding fun? {is_fun}")

# Try calculating with variables:
apples = 12
friends = 4
each_gets = apples // friends
print(f"If {apples} apples are shared among {friends} friends, each gets {each_gets}.")

challenge.title: Create a Student ID Card Output
challenge.description: Read a student's name and favorite subject using `input()`, or define variables, and print a greeting that includes both their name and the result of `7 * 8` (which is `56`). Specifically, write a program that takes a name via `input()` and prints `Hello <name>, 7 x 8 = 56`.
hints: Use `name = input()` to read the student's name.
challenge.solutionCode:
name = input("Enter student name: ")
result = 7 * 8
print(f"Hello {name}, 7 x 8 = {result}")

lessons.title: Interactive Programs with input()
lessons.summary: Pause execution and ask the user for live input over WebSocket using input(), int(), and float().
lessons.conceptHtml:
How input() Works

The input(prompt) function pauses your Python program, displays the prompt in the terminal, and waits for the user to type a response and press Enter.

  • input() always returns a string (str), even if the user types digits!
  • To do math with user input, convert it using int(input(...)) for whole numbers or float(input(...)) for decimals.
Converting Input to Numbers
age_text = input("Enter your age: ")
age = int(age_text)
print(f"In 5 years, you will be {age + 5} years old!")
lessons.starterCode:
# Lesson 2: Live Interactive input() over WebSocket
# Run this program and type your answers directly in the Terminal below!

name = input("What is your name? ")
print(f"Nice to meet you, {name}! 👋")

birth_year = int(input("What year were you born? "))
current_year = 2026
age = current_year - birth_year

print(f"Awesome! That makes you around {age} years old in {current_year}.")

# Let's add two numbers interactively:
print("\n--- Quick Addition Calculator ---")
num1 = float(input("Enter first number: "))
num2 = float(input("Enter second number: "))
print(f"{num1} + {num2} = {num1 + num2}")

challenge.title: Rectangle Area Calculator
challenge.description: Write a program that asks the user for `width` and `height` (as integers using two `input()` calls) and prints `Area: <result>` where `<result>` is `width * height`.
challenge.solutionCode:
width = int(input("Enter width: "))
height = int(input("Enter height: "))
area = width * height
print(f"Area: {area}")

lessons.title: Making Decisions (if / elif / else)
lessons.summary: Teach your program to make decisions and branch based on conditions and comparison operators.
lessons.conceptHtml:
Conditional Statements

Programs make decisions using if, elif (else if), and else. Remember that Python uses 4 spaces of indentation to group code inside a block!

  • Comparison operators: == (equal), != (not equal), >, <, >=, <=
  • Logical operators: and, or, not
Syntax
score = int(input("Enter exam score: "))
if score >= 90:
    print("Grade: A 🌟")
elif score >= 75:
    print("Grade: B 👍")
else:
    print("Keep practicing! 💪")

challenge.title: Even or Odd & Sign Checker
challenge.description: Read an integer from `input()`. If the number is divisible by 2 (`num % 2 == 0`), print `Even`, otherwise print `Odd`.
hints: Use the modulo operator `%` which gives the remainder of division.
`if num % 2 == 0:` means the number is Even.

lessons.title: Loops: for & while with input()
lessons.summary: Repeat actions automatically with for-loops and build interactive multi-step sessions with while-loops.
lessons.conceptHtml:
Repeating Code with Loops

Python provides two types of loops:

  • for i in range(start, stop): repeats a fixed number of times. Note that range(1, 6) produces 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
  • while condition: repeats as long as the condition remains True. Combine while with input() to build interactive games and menus!
Interactive while loop
secret = "python"
guess = ""
while guess != secret:
    guess = input("Guess the password: ").lower()
print("Access Granted! 🔓")
lessons.starterCode:
# Lesson 4: Loops (for & interactive while loop)

n = int(input("Enter a number for its multiplication table: "))
print(f"\n--- Multiplication Table of {n} ---")
for i in range(1, 6):
    print(f"{n} x {i} = {n * i}")

# Interactive Guessing Game using a while loop and input()!
print("\n🎯 Mini Number Guessing Game (Secret number is between 1 and 10)")
secret_number = 7
attempts = 0

while True:
    guess = int(input("Take a guess (1-10): "))
    attempts += 1
    if guess == secret_number:
        print(f"🎉 Correct! You found {secret_number} in {attempts} attempt(s)!")
        break
    elif guess < secret_number:
        print("Too low! Try higher ⬆️")
    else:
        print("Too high! Try lower ⬇️")

challenge.title: Sum of 1 to N
challenge.description: Read a positive integer `N` from `input()` and calculate the sum of all integers from `1` up to `N` (inclusive). Print `Sum: <total>`.
hints: Loop with `for i in range(1, n + 1):` and add `total += i`.
challenge.solutionCode:
n = int(input("Enter N: "))
total = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    total += i
print(f"Sum: {total}")

lessons.title: Lists & Dictionaries
lessons.summary: Store collections of items in ordered Lists and key-value pairs in Dictionaries.
lessons.conceptHtml:
Working with Collections

  • Lists [10, 20, 30] store ordered sequences. Use .append(item) to add, len(items) for count, and sum(items) to total numbers.
  • Dictionaries {"name": "Diya", "marks": 92} store key-value pairs for instant lookup by key.
List & Dictionary Example
fruits = ["Apple", "Mango"]
fruits.append("Banana")
for idx, fruit in enumerate(fruits, start=1):
    print(f"{idx}. {fruit}")
lessons.starterCode:
# Lesson 5: Lists & Dictionaries

cart = []
prices = {
    "notebook": 45,
    "pen": 15,
    "backpack": 650,
    "calculator": 320
}

print("🛒 Student Bookstore Catalog:")
for item, price in prices.items():
    print(f"  • {item.title():12} : ₹{price}")

choice = input("\nWhich item would you like to add to your cart? ").strip().lower()
qty = int(input("How many would you like to buy? "))

if choice in prices:
    unit_price = prices[choice]
    total_cost = unit_price * qty
    cart.append({"item": choice, "qty": qty, "total": total_cost})
    print(f"✅ Added {qty}x {choice.title()} — Total: ₹{total_cost}")
else:
    print(f"⚠️ '{choice}' is not in the catalog.")

challenge.title: Find Maximum and Average of 3 Numbers
challenge.description: Read 3 integers using three `input()` calls, store them in a list, and print `Max: <highest>` on one line and `Sum: <total>` on the next line.
challenge.solutionCode:
a = int(input("First number: "))
b = int(input("Second number: "))
c = int(input("Third number: "))
nums = [a, b, c]
print(f"Max: {max(nums)}")
print(f"Sum: {sum(nums)}")

lessons.title: Functions & Modular Code
lessons.summary: Organize reusable logic with def, parameters, return values, and docstrings.
lessons.conceptHtml:
Defining Functions with def

Functions let you write a block of code once and call it whenever you need it.

  • Use def function_name(parameters): to define a function.
  • Use return value to send the result back to the caller.
Function Example
def celsius_to_fahrenheit(c):
    return (c * 9 / 5) + 32

temp_c = float(input("Enter °C: "))
print(f"{temp_c}°C is {celsius_to_fahrenheit(temp_c):.1f}°F")

challenge.title: Square Function & Output
challenge.description: Define a function `square(n)` that returns `n * n`. Read an integer from `input()`, call `square(n)`, and print `Square: <result>`.
challenge.solutionCode:
def square(n):
    return n * n

val = int(input("Enter a number: "))
print(f"Square: {square(val)}")

lessons.title: Strings, Slicing & Palindromes
lessons.summary: Manipulate text with string methods, slicing [::-1], word counting, and pattern challenges.
lessons.conceptHtml:
String Power Tools

Python makes working with text effortless:

  • text.upper(), text.lower(), text.title(), text.strip()
  • text.split() splits a sentence into a list of words.
  • text[::-1] reverses a string using slice notation!
Reversing a String
word = "radar"
if word == word[::-1]:
    print("It's a palindrome!")
lessons.starterCode:
# Lesson 7: Strings, Slicing & Text Analysis

sentence = input("Type a sentence or word to analyze: ").strip()

words = sentence.split()
reversed_text = sentence[::-1]
vowel_count = sum(1 for ch in sentence.lower() if ch in "aeiou")

print("\n📊 Text Analysis Report:")
print(f"  • Character count : {len(sentence)}")
print(f"  • Word count      : {len(words)}")
print(f"  • Vowel count     : {vowel_count}")
print(f"  • Reversed        : {reversed_text}")

cleaned = "".join(ch.lower() for ch in sentence if ch.isalnum())
if cleaned and cleaned == cleaned[::-1]:
    print("  • ✨ This is a Palindrome!")
else:
    print("  • Not a palindrome.")

lessons.title: Error Handling (try / except) & Mini-Game
lessons.summary: Prevent crashes when users type invalid input using try/except blocks, and build a full interactive game!
lessons.conceptHtml:
Graceful Error Handling with try / except

What happens if your program runs int(input("Enter a number: ")) and the user types "hello"? Python raises a ValueError! You can catch and recover from errors using try and except:

Safe Number Input
try:
    num = int(input("Enter a number: "))
    print(f"100 / {num} = {100 / num}")
except ValueError:
    print("Please enter valid digits!")
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print("Cannot divide by zero!")
lessons.starterCode:
# Lesson 8: Safe Input Validation with try / except

print("🛡️ Safe Division Calculator")

while True:
    raw_a = input("\nEnter numerator (or 'q' to quit): ").strip()
    if raw_a.lower() == 'q':
        print("Goodbye! Keep coding in Python! 🐍")
        break

    raw_b = input("Enter denominator: ").strip()

    try:
        a = float(raw_a)
        b = float(raw_b)
        result = a / b
        print(f"✅ Result: {a} / {b} = {result:.2f}")
    except ValueError:
        print("❌ Error: Please enter valid numeric values!")
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        print("❌ Error: Division by zero is undefined!")

templates.name: 🎯 Interactive Quiz Game
templates.code:
# Interactive Python Quiz Game (Uses input() over WebSocket)
questions = [
    ("What keyword defines a function in Python?", "def"),
    ("Which function reads user input from the terminal?", "input"),
    ("What is the output of 2 ** 3 in Python?", "8")
]

print("=== 🧠 Welcome to the Python Mastery Quiz! ===")
student = input("Enter your name to begin: ").strip() or "Student"
score = 0

for idx, (q, ans) in enumerate(questions, start=1):
    print(f"\nQuestion {idx}: {q}")
    user_ans = input("Your answer: ").strip().lower()
    if user_ans == ans:
        print("✅ Correct!")
        score += 1
    else:
        print(f"❌ Not quite! The right answer was: {ans}")

print(f"\n🏆 Final Score for {student}: {score}/{len(questions)}")
